title: Model onboarding notary + continuous cost-signal publishing for verified performance manifests
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Goal: Create a hardened, signed performance manifest publishing flow that binds model binaries (and runtime-variant metadata) to Redwood-verified latency/throughput/cost signatures and continuously monitors cost drift. This ticket scopes the product spec, rollout policy, and high-level acceptance criteria for a model onboarding notary and a lightweight continuous cost-signal pipeline.

Background: Current verified profiles are produced during onboarding but lack a compact signed artifact that: 1) guarantees provenance (who verified, which git commit/artifact), 2) embeds variant hints (quantization, kernel family, batch targets) and 3) carries automated canary/publish rules. Operations want a manifest that's machine-readable and auditable, while platform teams want clear rollback triggers for cost and latency regressions.

Primary deliverables:
- Signed performance manifest schema (compact YAML+signature) that includes: model_id, model_version, artifact_sha, runtime_variant_hints, sampled_latency_p95, throughput_rps, normalized_cost_per_1k_tokens, verification_run_id, verifier_identity, publish_constraints (canary_pct, min_samples), and optional fallback_variants.
- Notary service design: sign manifests using customer-/org-level keys via KMS; store signatures in a canonical registry (git-backed ledger + object store).
- Publish pipeline: from verification job -> sign manifest -> store artifact -> trigger registry publish and create canary rollout plan that integrates with routing.
- Continuous cost-signal monitor (sampled): a lightweight service that consumes production telemetry, maps traffic to a manifest version, calculates rolling cost deltas and alerts/publishes drift events back to registry.
- Rollback matrix and auto-fallback policy: threshold-based rules (e.g., >10% cost increase OR >20% latency regression on p95 across 5k samples) to trigger automated partial rollback to a compatible variant.

Acceptance criteria:
- Manifest schema approved by Security and Runtime teams.
- Notary can sign and verify manifests locally in CI and via KMS in staging.
- End-to-end demo: onboarding job produces signed manifest, pushes to registry, and a routing canary receives 0.5% traffic.
- Continuous cost-signal detects an injected cost bump in staging and surfaces an alert in Console and creates a rollback ticket.
- Documentation: PRD + publishing runbook + operator playbook published to Confluence.

Trade-offs and decisions to evaluate:
- Signature format: lean HMAC vs full PKI (we propose PKI-signed manifests with KMS-stored private keys to allow cross-service verification).
- Storage: git-backed ledger (good audit trail) vs scalable object store (S3) for binary artifacts; propose hybrid: git index for manifest metadata + S3 for attached artifacts.
- Canary sizing: tight canaries reduce risk but increase validation time; propose 0.5% for fast feedback with sampled shadow traffic for throughput signals.

Open questions:
- How to represent quantization/compile hints without exploding schema complexity? (We will allow a freeform "variant_hints" map limited to 8 k/v pairs.)
- Should cost drift trigger immediate rollback or an automated gated rollback requiring on-call approval? (Default: automated partial rollback for >20% user-facing latency regressions; for cost-only regressions, create high-priority alert and auto-scale fallback if available.)

comments: 2025-11-06 - Asha Patel: Kickoff with product, runtime, and security. Agreed to pursue signed manifests and a hybrid storage approach. Liam volunteered to own engineering delivery.

2025-11-20 - Morgan Chen (Security): Require PKI with per-team keys and an allowlist for verifier identities. Added requirement for signature revocation metadata.

2025-11-27 - Priya Rao (Runtime): Variant_hints schema looks OK; asked to ensure runtime can reconcile hints with kernel selection without extra network calls. We'll add hash of compiled-variant to manifest.

2025-12-12 - Asha Patel: Product review notes - add clarity on customer opt-out for auto-rollback and document how dedicated customers can pin to org-level keys. Updated acceptance criteria to include opt-out docs.
